excerpt: The review reports that detection and discrimination of near-threshold visual stimuli are inversely related to pre-stimulus alpha amplitude, and that participants with greater tonic alpha levels in a sustained-attention task had larger LP1 components, with that relationship predicting task performance.
overview: Performance correlations make the alpha pattern behaviorally consequential. The evidence indicates that alpha level is not merely an electrophysiological by-product; it tracks perceptual sensitivity and attentional success. These are correlational findings, so they establish prediction and functional relevance but require causal manipulation for stronger mechanistic inference.
title: Alpha Predicts Performance
